cleanIntro: This guide follows Bul Armory's SAS II owner's manual. That book is written for the SAS II and never prints "Ultralight", so check your variant against it. Its takedown has no barrel bushing and no recoil spring plug to turn: the slide stop comes out at the disassembly notch, the slide runs forward off the frame, and the guide rod, recoil spring and plug come out of the slide as one assembly once a bent paper clip holds the spring compressed. Wear safety glasses for the whole strip. Bul stops at the barrel and says nothing past it is needed for regular maintenance.

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: This guide follows Bul Armory's SAS II manual, which does not name the Ultralight, so check your variant against it. Point the pistol in a safe direction, press the magazine release on the left side of the frame and take the magazine out. Put safety glasses on now: the recoil spring comes out of this pistol under compression.
steps.prose: Bul's disassembly begins with the pistol completely unloaded, and the magazine is the first thing out.
steps.quote: 1. Make sure the magazine is removed.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 1, PDF p.11 (the book prints no page numbers)
steps.warn: Always make sure the pistol is completely unloaded before disassembly. Wear safety glasses in case you lose control of a spring-loaded component, which could injure your eyes.

steps.title: Slide back, look in the chamber
steps.action: Pull the slide all the way back and look into the chamber to confirm it is empty. A round in the chamber stays there when the magazine comes out, so this look is what actually proves the pistol empty.
steps.prose: Bul's own rule: if the slide is not locked open with the empty chamber exposed, treat the pistol as loaded.
steps.quote: 2. Clear the firearm by pulling the slide to the rear and visually inspecting the chamber.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 2, PDF p.11

steps.title: Slide forward, hammer down to rest
steps.action: With the chamber confirmed empty, let the slide go forward and lower the hammer to its rest position: fully down, resting directly against the slide. Lower it under control rather than letting it fall.
steps.prose: Do not leave the hammer at half cock. Bul's at-rest position is the hammer all the way down against the slide.
steps.quote: Allow the slide to travel forward and lower the hammer to its rest position.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 2, PDF p.11

steps.title: Slide back to the disassembly notch and hold it
steps.action: Draw the slide back until the checkered rear of the slide release lines up with the small disassembly notch on the slide, and hold the slide there.
steps.prose: The slide stop only comes out at this one slide position. If it will not move in the next step, the notch is not lined up yet.
steps.quote: 3. Pull the slide rearward until the checkered rear of the slide release is lined up with the small disassembly notch on the slide (Fig 11) and hold in place.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 3, PDF p.11

steps.title: Push the shaft from the right, slide stop out the left
steps.action: Still holding the slide at the notch, push the end of the slide stop shaft where it shows on the right side of the frame, then pull the slide stop out of the left side.
steps.prose: The book prints "right slide of the frame"; it means the right side. Keep your grip on the slide: once the stop is out, only your hand holds it against the recoil spring.
steps.quote: 4. Push the slide stop shaft on the right slide of the frame (Fig 12) and remove the slide stop from the left side of the frame (Fig 13).
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 4, PDF p.11

steps.title: Ease the slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Let the slide run forward slowly under your hand and take it off the front of the frame. The barrel and the recoil assembly come away inside it.
steps.prose: Do not let the slide snap forward. The recoil spring is driving it.
steps.quote: 5. Slowly allow the slide to move forward and remove from the frame
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 5, PDF p.11

steps.title: Push the guide rod forward until its hole shows
steps.action: With the slide upside down in your hand, push the guide rod forward toward the muzzle to compress the recoil spring, until the hole in the guide rod is exposed. Keep it there.
steps.prose: The spring is fully loaded at this point. Keep your safety glasses on and the rod under control.
steps.quote: the recoil spring can be compressed by pushing the guide rod forward toward the muzzle until the hole on the guide rod is exposed.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 6, PDF p.11

steps.title: Bent paper clip into the hole
steps.action: Bend 5/16 inch of the end of a paper clip to a right angle and push the bent end into the exposed hole in the guide rod. The clip now holds the spring compressed so the assembly can come out in one piece.
steps.prose: Make the clip before you compress the spring, so you are not bending wire with one hand on a loaded rod.
steps.quote: A paper clip with 5/16" of its end bent at a 90-degree angle can be inserted into the hole
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 6, PDF p.12

steps.title: Recoil assembly out the back of the slide
steps.action: With the spring and plug held by the clip, draw the whole recoil assembly toward the rear of the slide and lift it out. Leave the clip in place while it is out.
steps.prose: Taking the clip out now would free the spring. It stays in until the assembly is back in the slide on reassembly.
steps.quote: With the guide spring and plug now depressed, the assembly can be removed by drawing it toward the rear of the slide.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 6, PDF p.12

steps.title: Swing the barrel link down
steps.action: Swivel the barrel link down until it lies parallel with the barrel.
steps.prose: The barrel will not slide out with the link standing up.
steps.quote: 7. Swivel the barrel link to its downward position parallel with the barrel.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 7, PDF p.12

steps.title: Barrel forward out of the slide
steps.action: Slide the barrel forward through the barrel housing at the front of the slide and take it out.
steps.prose: There is no bushing to turn on this pistol; the barrel comes straight out the front.
steps.quote: The barrel can now be removed by sliding it forward through the barrel housing.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, Step 7, PDF p.12

steps.title: Field strip complete: Bul stops here
steps.action: That is the field strip: frame, slide, slide stop, barrel, and the recoil assembly held by its paper clip. Bul Armory takes the pistol no further for cleaning.
steps.prose: The book's disassembly ends here and reassembles by reversing these steps.
steps.quote: Further disassembly is not recommended and not necessary for regular maintenance.
steps.cite: BUL SAS/1911 instruction and safety manual — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — DISASSMBLING THE BUL SAS II, PDF p.12
steps.warn: DO NOT alter any parts or add or replace parts on your own. Always let only a qualified gunsmith work on your pistol.

deepAbsentReason: Bul Armory's SAS II manual ends at the field strip. After the barrel comes out it says: "Further disassembly is not recommended and not necessary for regular maintenance." (PDF p.12). The book gives no firing pin, extractor or frame procedure, so this guide has no deep lane.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Cleaning rod, brass bristle brush and patches sized for your pistol's caliber
Good-quality cleaning solution swabbed through the bore
All excess solvent wiped away afterwards
⛔ Never fire with oil, grease or anything else even partly obstructing the bore

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME RAILS
tasks: Cleaning solution swabbed on the slide and frame rails
Do not leave powder solvent on blued steel parts for long: it can dissolve bluing
Hard-chrome model: oil and maintain it as if it were blue steel

cleaning.name: OIL
tasks: Light oil on the whole pistol: barrel, slide rail cuts, frame rails, trigger and hammer assemblies
Light coat of rust preventative wiped over all external surfaces
Do not over-oil: dust and debris trapped in oil form a gum that in time causes misfires
Do not spray or apply lubricants directly on ammunition

reassembly: Bul's instruction is to reverse the disassembly.
Barrel back in through the barrel housing at the front of the slide, link swung down.

Recoil assembly, still held by its paper clip, back in from the rear of the slide; push the guide rod forward a little to take the load off the clip, pull the clip out and let the spring take up under control.
Slide back onto the frame and drawn rearward until the disassembly notch lines up with the slide release.
Slide stop back in from the left side of the frame, its shaft through the barrel link, then let the slide go forward.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber empty, muzzle in a safe direction. Work the slide by hand several times and check it runs fully forward and back without binding and that the slide stop sits flush in the frame. Cock the hammer fully, push the thumb safety up into its notch on the slide and back down again; Bul's instruction is that the hammer is fully cocked before the safety goes up. If anything did not go back the way it came out, Bul's own instruction is to let only a qualified gunsmith work on the pistol.
